bloc.C'est la question qui commande toutes le: This is the question that governs all the others. The Regulation does not only classify systems, it allocates obligations among operators: the same system can be high-risk for everyone and bind each of them only for their own part. The provider carries Articles # to #; the deployer Article #; the importer Article #; the distributor Article #. Answering “provider” when you are a deployer produces an entirely wrong list of obligations.
bloc.Ce sont des exceptions : n'en cochez auc: These are exceptions: tick none if none applies — the system is then within scope. The Regulation does not apply to systems used exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes, to those developed for the sole purpose of scientific research, to research and testing before placing on the market (testing in real-world conditions is not excluded), or to the obligations of deployers who are natural persons using the system for a strictly personal purpose.
bloc.Chacune de ces trois situations fait de: Each of these three situations makes you the provider of the system, whatever role you declared above — and transfers to you all the obligations of Articles # to #. This is the reclassification organisations discover latest, often after fine-tuning a purchased model.
bloc.Cochez tout ce qui s'applique. Une prati: Tick everything that applies. A recognised practice makes the system prohibited: it can be neither placed on the market, nor put into service, nor used. Points (ba) and (bb) apply from # December # (Regulation (EU) #/#).
bloc.Dispositifs médicaux, jouets, ascenseurs: Medical devices, toys, lifts, radio equipment, pressure equipment, recreational craft, gas appliances… High risk requires two cumulative conditions: a safety component (or the product itself) and a third-party conformity assessment.
bloc.Il infère, à partir des entrées reçues,: It infers, from the input it receives, how to generate its outputs
bloc.La définition compte sept éléments, et i: The definition has seven elements, and they are cumulative. Tick those that describe your system. Software that applies hand-written rules, without inferring anything, is not an AI system — and the Regulation does not apply to it at all. This is the first possible exit from scope, and the least often checked.
bloc.Le règlement exempte partiellement ce qu: The Regulation partially exempts what is distributed under a free and open-source licence — but only free of charge. The next question decides whether the exemption really holds, and it must be asked before you count on it.
bloc.Les systèmes à haut risque de l'annexe I: Annex III high-risk systems already on the market at the date of application only move into the full regime if their design changes significantly. The date used here is the one in the timetable shown at the top of this page: # December #, set by the Digital Omnibus for Annex III.
bloc.Une seule réponse positive fait tomber l: A single positive answer removes the exemption, whatever the licence. This is the point on which the “open source” exemption is most often wrongly invoked: the licence is indeed free, but the model is monetised elsewhere. Tick only what is true.

bloc.💡 Conseil : Distinguer la personnalisati: 💡 Tip: Distinguish legitimate personalisation (Art. # → transparency) from manipulative practices (Art. # → prohibition). The line can be thin depending on the techniques used.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Distinguer les usages intern: 💡 Tip: Distinguish internal uses from published content — only the latter triggers the disclosure obligation.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Documenter quelles données s: 💡 Tip: Document which data is accessible — a poorly partitioned RAG agent can expose sensitive data.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Informer explicitement les s: 💡 Tip: Inform employees explicitly before any deployment — the combined AI Act + GDPR + employment law regime makes this case particularly exposed to legal challenges.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Interroger les achats et l'I: 💡 Tip: Ask procurement and IT about the AI options already switched on in SaaS contracts.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Le médecin reste responsable: 💡 Tip: The physician remains responsible for the final decision — AI cannot replace clinical judgement. Document the chain of responsibility explicitly.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Les établissements d'enseign: 💡 Tip: Educational institutions are often unaware of their status as high-risk deployers when they use third-party assessment or guidance tools.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Prioriser dans le Registre —: 💡 Tip: Prioritise in the register — high risk of employment tribunal litigation.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Vérifier en premier si l'usa: 💡 Tip: First check whether the intended use falls under the prohibited practices of Art. # — before even talking about high-risk compliance.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Vérifier la compatibilité RG: 💡 Tip: Check compatibility with GDPR Art. # (right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing) — this case combines two regulatory regimes.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Vérifier que la mention appa: 💡 Tip: Check that the notice appears from the very first message, not only in the legal notices.
bloc.💡 Conseil : Vérifier si votre organisati: 💡 Tip: Check whether your organisation is an operator of essential importance (OIE) or of importance (OII) within the meaning of NIS # — the combined AI Act + NIS # regime is particularly demanding.
